label: copy-phase input z (fed-back z), from the 3rd copied position on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is z, i.e. the model just output z and it is fed back in. Every copy-phase z input at recall_idx >= 2 activates it (dev precision 1.0), and these cover ~99.9% of activation mass. When z is fed back at recall_idx 1 (z was original token 0), it fires on only some of those cases and weakly (~0.55-0.75 of max). Later positions reach ~0.8-1.0 of max, with the largest values late in long sequences. Never fires on z during the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token (only a few dozen stray activations). Does not depend on which token is being output, on L, or on digit count.

issues: The predicate holds up on test: precision 1.0, recall 0.964, F1 0.982, mass recall 0.999, and 0 false positives. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase. Only about 21 dev activations fall on input tokens other than z. Out_tok, prev_tok, next_out, L and n_digits show no structure beyond what the predicate already covers. It also does not depend on whether the model is copying correctly: correct==0 rows carry about 5e-5 of mass.

The magnitude claim for recall_idx 1 is wrong. The explanation says z fed back at recall_idx 1 fires at about 0.55-0.75 of max. In fact the recall_idx==1 activations are tiny: misses on both dev and test show 0.01-0.10 of max (for example 'z t d p t c <DEL> [z:0.08]'). They carry 0.14% of mass and fall only in the lowest quartile. They fire on just 16.6% of those steps (test precision 0.166).

The 0.55-0.75 band actually belongs to recall_idx 2, where z was original token 1. Lowest-quartile examples include 'a z x k n b <DEL> a [z:0.57]' and '1 z b g f w <DEL> 1 [z:0.56]', and one top example shows '[z:0.45]' at recall_idx 2. On test, 78% of the lowest activation quartile is recall_idx==2. So the claim that 'later positions reach about 0.8-1.0' is only true from roughly recall_idx 3 on.

Magnitude rises steadily with recall_idx (how late in the copy the fed-back z sits). On test, recall_idx==2 makes up 78% of quartile 1. recall_idx==3 makes up 62% of quartile 2. recall_idx==5 makes up 22-28% of quartiles 3-4. recall_idx==8 is almost entirely in quartile 4. The explanation's 'largest values late in long sequences' is consistent with this, but it should be stated as a steady rise with copy position.

The label's phrase 'from the 3rd copied position on' is ambiguous and arguably off by one. At recall_idx 2 the input is original token 1, which is the 2nd token fed back. It is clearer to say z was original token k >= 1.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase fed-back z, where z was original token 1 or later (recall_idx >= 2); magnitude rises steadily with copy position (about 0.55-0.75 of max at recall_idx 2, about 0.9-1.0 late); near-zero, sporadic firing (0.01-0.1 of max) when z was original token 0
